title: What Are the Research Trends in Social Work Regarding Social Intervention in Migration Matters? A Bibliometric Analysis (2012-2021)
authors: Zárate-Rueda, Ruth; Villamizar-Niño, Yazmin; Beltrán-Villamizar, Yolima Ivonne
abstract: <jats:p>This study aims to analyze research trends related to social intervention in migration issues by Social Work, during the period 2012-2021. A three-phase bibliometric analysis was performed, as follows: (i) literature review, (ii) document collection, (iii) interpretation and visualization of maps. In addition, the database Web of Science and the software VOSviewer were selected to map co-occurrence, co-citation and co-authorship networks. In the results, the countries, authors and journals with the highest number of publications were identified. Among them, the United States stands out, with studies on immigration from the global South, besides methodological components defined by external referents and trends on human rights, mental health, childhood and adolescence. It was concluded that professional practice requires taking on new challenges from a transformative intervention, assuming scientific rationality and an interpretation of social reality.</jats:p>
